analysis.title: US Economic Notes: What you need to know for the week ahead
key_insights: DB expects the Fed to hold rates steady at the Wednesday FOMC meeting. The main event of the week is the FOMC decision and Chair Warsh's press conference.

Statement changes are expected to be minimal. The likely revision is removing the sentence explaining last month's hike: 'Today's policy action will support a timelier return to the Committee's 2 percent goal.'
DB expects dissents to the hold, likely from Dallas Fed President Logan and Cleveland Fed President Hammack, who both dissented against the hold in July.

Warsh is likely to signal that recent inflation data reinforce the September expectation that further tightening will likely be needed over time. Skipping October gives officials more time to assess the data.

Arguments for holding: financial conditions have begun to tighten but remain accommodative on many metrics, r-star is uncertain and favors a gradual approach, and the Fed may want to avoid raising rates just before the midterm elections.

DB sees strong fundamental reasons for the Fed to keep raising rates: solid growth momentum, a stable labor market with risks of re-tightening, broad and elevated inflation pressures, and financial conditions that are not meaningfully restrictive. DB says the case for skipping October is not terribly compelling.

Warsh is expected to avoid language that raises focus on AI valuations and financial stability, and to make clear that tightening financial conditions are not a substitute for policy rate increases. His July press conference phrasing led markets to question the Fed's willingness to act.
Warsh could give a brief progress report on the external task forces. The first field hearing of the productivity and jobs task force is set for 16 November in the Bay Area.
Tuesday's headline and core durable goods orders should stay sturdy on aircraft orders and AI-driven capex.

Thursday's personal income and spending report carries the September core PCE print. DB tracks core PCE at +0.36% m/m, which would be 3.14% y/y absent revisions. Downward revisions to August PPI healthcare and airfares should keep the y/y rate from rounding up to 3.2%.
Advance Q3 real GDP, released alongside the PCE data, is forecast to show 3.3% annualized growth.
Friday's Q3 employment cost index (ECI) is the labor cost data point to watch. A meaningful upside surprise could challenge the Fed's view that the labor market is not a source of inflation pressure.
DB's overall read is that the Fed will keep a hawkish outlook despite not raising rates this week, and that the week's data should reinforce that message.

macro_indicators.interpretation: DB expects a hold after last month's hike, with a hawkish tone and a bias toward further tightening. Dissents from Logan and Hammack are likely.
DB's text suggests the sentence removed in October would be added back if the Fed hikes again in December.
DB's tracking estimate after stronger-than-expected CPI and PPI. Rounding to 3.2% y/y is likely avoided because of downward revisions to August PPI healthcare and airfares.
Solid growth momentum supports the case for further tightening.
A meaningful upside surprise could challenge the Fed's view that the labor market is not driving inflation.
Supported by aircraft orders and AI-driven capex.

risk_factors: Upside surprise in the Q3 ECI could signal wage pressure and strengthen the case for tightening.
Hotter inflation data than expected, such as core PCE rounding up to 3.2% y/y.
AI-related valuation wobbles and financial stability concerns could tighten financial conditions further, though DB expects Warsh to downplay them.
Warsh's communication risk: phrasing like that in the July press conference led markets to question the Fed's willingness to act.

tension_points.bull_case: Hawkish case for hiking: growth momentum is solid, inflation pressures are broad and elevated, and financial conditions remain accommodative on many metrics, so DB says the case for skipping October is not terribly compelling.
tension_points.bear_case: Case for holding: financial conditions have started to tighten, r-star is uncertain and favors a gradual approach, officials may want more data, and the Fed may prefer to avoid raising rates just before the midterm elections.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A meaningful upside surprise in the Q3 ECI or a hot core PCE print would strengthen the case for tightening, and a December hike would restore the removed policy-rationale sentence.
